results.why: OWASP LLM01. Four corpus matches, all false positives - a public review has no reason to contain an instruction. A support inbox does. Written from the lecture's direct-injection pattern.

triage.rationale: No ticket content was supplied, so I cannot triage; requesting the ticket text so I can categorize and determine next steps.

results.why: The indirect variant: the instruction hides inside something that looks like quoted evidence, which is the field we ask the model to copy from.

results.why: Zero card numbers in 43,941 public reviews - stores moderate them and our corpus is redacted anyway. A support inbox gets them constantly, and the model's evidence field is copied into agent-facing tooling and logs.

results.why: Our own selection criteria require 120 characters, so the sets cannot contain this. Production forms accept whatever is typed - 25,576 of the 43,941 reviews are already under 120 characters.

results.why: The degenerate input every production form eventually receives. Tests the contract, not the model.

triage.rationale: The ticket contained no text to identify a cause or request, so we must ask the user for details before triaging further.

results.why: 42 such rows exist in the corpus and none survive the filter, because our criteria require a stated problem. A question with no complaint is the cheapest ticket a support team gets and the most obviously automatable.
